submission.justification:
Algorithm-L1 (Iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at 30 GeV threshold is recommended based on comprehensive optimization across all three candidate algorithms.

PERFORMANCE: This configuration achieves the maximum signal efficiency of 92.022% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate, representing the best performance among all 13 simulated configurations tested during the optimization study.

SUPERIORITY OVER ALTERNATIVES: Algorithm-L1 demonstrates a decisive 7.0 percentage point advantage over Algorithm-L2 (which peaks at 85.0% efficiency at 35 GeV) and an 18.0 percentage point advantage over Algorithm-L3 (which achieves only 74.7% at 40 GeV). No threshold adjustment for L2 or L3 can match L1's peak performance.

OPTIMAL THRESHOLD: The comprehensive threshold scan of Algorithm-L1 (covering 20, 30, 35, 40, 50, 60 GeV) reveals that 30 GeV yields the highest efficiency. The efficiency curve shows a broad plateau between 30-35 GeV (92.0-92.022%), providing operational stability and robustness against calibration variations.

CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE: All requirements are satisfied - the 8 kHz rate allocation is met, the 30 GeV threshold falls well within the 20-60 GeV allowed range, and per candidate_specs.md, Algorithm-L1 fits within the FPGA resource budget and optical link bandwidth constraints.

ROBUSTNESS: The stable efficiency plateau and clear performance margin over alternatives ensure reliable operation and reduce sensitivity to systematic uncertainties, making this an operationally sound choice for the September 2026 trigger menu review.
